journal_text: I came to Claywater Station on the Blackwood Road. Travellers there pay Livia Varinius, the well-keeper, 2 drakes for the stop this season. Signs-For-The-Cargo, the landing's poler, now wants 1 drake from every walker who wades the ford. I'm to hear each keeper's side. Claywater Station is about 640 yards west of the signpost at Cartwright's Cross on the Blackwood Road, where the arms point to Gideon and to Leyawiin. Going west, a painted pole barrier stands in a field about 110 yards off the road on the right; that is the Drowning Gate. The station house roof shows about 100 yards on, ahead on the left. Livia Varinius keeps the well at the station house door, inside the low stone walls. Signs-For-The-Cargo poles the plank raft at the landing stage across the ford in the morning, about 65 yards north of the well. The round mud huts stand behind it on the far bank. If the road runs on into open marsh with no roofs in sight, I have passed it.
directions: From the Blackwood Road: Claywater Station is about 640 yards west of the signpost at Cartwright's Cross, where the arms point to Gideon and to Leyawiin. Going west, a painted pole barrier stands in a field about 110 yards off the road on the right; that is the Drowning Gate, and the station house roof shows about 100 yards on, ahead on the left. The well stands at the station house door, inside the low stone walls. From the well, the raft and the landing stage are about 65 yards to the north, across the ford, with the round mud huts behind them on the far bank. If the road runs on into open marsh with no roofs in sight, you have passed it.

journal_text: At Claywater Station, Livia Varinius told me she raised the station's charge to 2 drakes to pay a mason to re-line the cracked well in stone. Signs-For-The-Cargo told me the landing began charging walkers at the ford. The landing worked this ford before the well was dug. The landing will not haul stone for the station. Signs-For-The-Cargo says a crocodile has taken the landing's clay cut below the ford. The landing will hear terms only from whoever wins back the cut before the rains. I'm to kill the crocodile and bring back the clay basket that lies at the cut. The cut is below the ford on the station bank. From the well, I go about 45 yards west, outside the low stone walls, to where the river swings west under a bare clay bank and the water lies deep and dark. If the bank flattens into reeds, I have gone past it. Signs-For-The-Cargo says Takes-The-Short-Weight can tell what ails the station's water. She lives in the round mud hut on the landing bank, about 30 yards north of the raft. In the morning she sits at the landing's fire, about 50 yards north of the raft.
directions: The clay cut is below the ford on the station bank: from the well, go about 45 yards west, outside the low stone walls, to where the river swings west under a bare clay bank and the water lies deep and dark. If the bank flattens into reeds, you have gone past it. Takes-The-Short-Weight lives in the round mud hut on the landing bank, about 30 yards north of the raft; in the morning she sits at the landing's fire, about 50 yards north of the raft.

journal_text: I killed the crocodile at the clay cut below the ford at Claywater Station and have the landing's clay basket. I'm to put terms to Livia Varinius and to Signs-For-The-Cargo before the rains: one charge of 2 drakes a stop, 1 to each bank, with the landing's clay rammed in behind the cracked lining. Livia Varinius says a mason's lining will mend the well and mud has no place in it. She says the landing would take half a charge for water it never draws. I'm to find out whether the well has cracked before. Takes-The-Short-Weight can taste the station's water if I bring it to her in Livia Varinius's dipper. Signs-For-The-Cargo says the station only wants stone. He will not haul it. Livia Varinius is at the well in the morning, at the counter by the station house door in the afternoon and at the stable at dusk. Signs-For-The-Cargo poles the raft in the morning and is at the drying racks behind it in the afternoon.
directions: Livia Varinius is at the well in the morning, at the counter by the station house door in the afternoon and at the stable at dusk; Signs-For-The-Cargo poles the raft in the morning and is at the drying racks behind it in the afternoon.

journal_text: I brought Livia Varinius and Signs-For-The-Cargo to terms at Claywater Station: one charge of 2 drakes a stop, 1 to each bank. The landing has rammed its clay in behind the cracked lining before the rains. I killed the crocodile at the clay cut and gave the landing back its basket. Livia Varinius will send for no mason. Travellers no longer have a reason to wade below the cut at night. The ferry at the Drowning Gate is free to me from now on.

I found that travellers at Claywater Station paid Livia Varinius at the well and again at the ford. I paid Signs-For-The-Cargo 100 drakes to take no charge from walkers this season, so they pay once, at the well. The well is still cracked.

I found that travellers at Claywater Station paid Livia Varinius at the well and again at the ford. I also found that the well's lining has cracked and been mended every year. To keep that quiet, Livia Varinius has dropped her charge back to the old drake. Signs-For-The-Cargo has dropped the walkers' charge in answer. Livia Varinius will send for no mason. The well is still cracked. The ferry at the Drowning Gate is free to me from now on.
The rains came to Claywater Station before I made terms between Livia Varinius and Signs-For-The-Cargo. The well is still cracked. Travellers still pay at both banks or wade below the ford at night.

Livia Varinius is dead. The well at Claywater Station has no keeper now. The station's charge ended with her. Signs-For-The-Cargo keeps the landing's charge on the ford. The two charges cannot be settled now.
Signs-For-The-Cargo is dead. The raft at Claywater Station has no poler. The landing will make no terms with Livia Varinius and the station while it mourns. Both charges stand.
Mee-Sei, who cooks at the fire stand in Greenspring, told me that guests at the lodge have been falling sick, and that people blame his food. I'm to find out what is making them ill.
directions: The pool lies under the Hist, a few steps from the fire stand; the lodge, where the sick guests lie, faces it across the spring.

journal_text: The guests at the Greenspring lodge sicken from the spring, not from Mee-Sei's food. Only Im-Moro, the spring-keeper, may go into the pool under the Hist. I'm to get into the pool, with her leave or without it at night.
directions: The stone lip is on the lodge side of the pool; the Hist's roots go down into the water on the far side.

journal_text: I have gone into the pool under the Hist at Greenspring. I'm to search the spring's throat between the roots, where the water comes up.

A dead man lies staked in the throat of the spring at Greenspring, his wrists tied with rope, the stake left blank. That is what sickens the guests. I'm to find out who he was and who killed him, before the killer leaves.
directions: The lodge store is the locked room behind Haj-Tei's door; Reeh-Shaal sleeps in the lodge and goes to the stone lip after the lamps are out.

journal_text: The courier who vanished from the Greenspring lodge twelve days ago lies in the spring, and what I have found points to Reeh-Shaal, the guest who says she waits for a boat to Helstrom. I'm to confront her with what I hold, and I need two things to make it stand.

I named Reeh-Shaal before the people of Greenspring as the one who killed the Helstrom courier and staked him in the spring. Im-Moro has had the body raised and given to the Hist, and the root-herald holds Reeh-Shaal for Helstrom.
Reeh-Shaal is dead by my hand at Greenspring. Im-Moro has had the courier's body raised from the spring, and the guests should mend.
I took the sealed packet from Reeh-Shaal at Greenspring and let her go. Nobody there will learn who killed the courier.
I accused Tsono-Ra of the courier's murder at Greenspring, and I was wrong. The village has closed ranks against me, and Reeh-Shaal has taken the boat.
Reeh-Shaal has left Greenspring on the Helstrom boat. Whoever killed the courier in the spring has gone, and the guests are still sick.

I came to in the hold of a broker's barge at Dock1, Lilmoth, among an Owing gang. Wuleen-Sei, the overseer, is reading the roll aloud, each name, the months owed and the months added for food, and my line is blank. I'm to answer her when she reaches it.
directions: The hold is the barge's one room below the deck; its door leads up to the plank and the pier of Dock1, Lilmoth.

journal_text: I gave Wuleen-Sei a name in the hold of the broker's barge at Dock1, Lilmoth, and she said it back for Ux-Xeek to call with the rest. At the foot of the plank Buys-The-Months, the broker, was looking the gang over from the pier. I'm to go up the plank with the gang and start along the shore.
directions: The plank runs from the hold's one door up to the pier of Dock1, where the broker stands at its foot; the shore path starts at the pier's landward end.

journal_text: I said nothing when Wuleen-Sei read my blank line in the hold of the broker's barge at Dock1, Lilmoth, and she read it blank again and passed on. At the foot of the plank Buys-The-Months, the broker, was looking the gang over from the pier. I'm to go up the plank with the gang and start along the shore.
directions: The plank runs from the hold's one door up to the pier of Dock1, where the broker stands at its foot; the shore path starts at the pier's landward end.

journal_text: I told Wuleen-Sei in the hold of the broker's barge at Dock1, Lilmoth, what she could do with her roll, and Ux-Xeek laughed once and stopped. At the foot of the plank Buys-The-Months, the broker, was looking the gang over from the pier. I'm to go up the plank with the gang and start along the shore.
directions: The plank runs from the hold's one door up to the pier of Dock1, where the broker stands at its foot; the shore path starts at the pier's landward end.

journal_text: Wuleen-Sei marched the gang up the plank of the barge at Dock1, Lilmoth, past Buys-The-Months, the broker on the pier, and out along the shore. A man called Mee-Tuja rides with us and says nothing of whom he serves. I'm to walk with the gang along the shore path, north and west past the paddies, to the camp the families keep at the edge of Hereguard Plantation.
directions: From the plank at Dock1 the shore path runs north and west along the water, past the first of the rice dikes; the camp is the cluster of huts on the reed bank at the paddy edge, where the path meets the reeds and the water goes shallow. If the path is lost, the paddy dikes of Hereguard Plantation lie always on the left hand.

journal_text: The gang's camp at the paddy edge of Hereguard Plantation is a few huts, a hatching shed, grave-stakes and the families' Hist cutting on its roots, with their clutch beneath it. Sal-Sei, the clutch-keeper, wants the evening bedding reed gathered for the shed; Deesh-Duun is in the huts and Ties-The-Loose-Plank at his rowboat. I'm to help Sal-Sei, hear about the cutting, and be at the fire when Wuleen-Sei reads the roll again.
directions: The shed stands beside the cutting at the camp's far end, under the grave-stakes; the bedding reed grows on the bank between the huts and the water.

journal_text: At dusk, as Wuleen-Sei read the roll at the camp's fire, a tall Argonian woman with a knotted cord at her wrist came in off the water with three of her people, killed the courier Mee-Tuja, took his satchel and looked at me, and left. The roll went into the fire. Her people are at the cutting and the huts are burning. Sal-Sei is at the shed, Deesh-Duun is in the burning huts, and Ties-The-Loose-Plank is at the rowboat. I'm to reach one of them; I cannot reach all three.
directions: The shed is at the camp's far end beside the cutting; the burning huts are between the shed and the fire; the rowboat lies on the water side, below the grave-stakes. The fire is the clock.

journal_text: I ran for the hatching shed at the camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge. Two of the woman's people have cut the roots that tie the cutting to the clutch and are filling jars with its sap, and Sal-Sei is on the ground beside the eggs. Behind me the huts have fallen in where Deesh-Duun was, and the rowboat is gone with Ties-The-Loose-Plank. I'm to drive the cutters off or slip past them and get Sal-Sei out through the reeds to the shore.
directions: From the shed the reeds run south to the shore below the camp, the way the families fish at night; keep the burning huts on the left hand.

journal_text: I went into the burning huts at the camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge and pulled Deesh-Duun out through the shallows. She saw the woman with the knotted cord as closely as I did. From the water I saw the cutters leave the shed with jars of sap, and Sal-Sei did not come out; the rowboat went off with Ties-The-Loose-Plank, or without him. I'm to bring Deesh-Duun round the burning end of the camp to the shore.
directions: The shore is south of the huts; keep to the water and the burning end of the camp stays on the left hand.

journal_text: I ran to the rowboat at the water side of the camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge, where one of the woman's people had Ties-The-Loose-Plank pinned, and got him into the boat. Behind me the huts have fallen in where Deesh-Duun was, and I did not reach Sal-Sei at the shed. I'm to pole the rowboat across the shallows to the shore below the camp.
directions: The rowboat lies on the water side of the camp below the grave-stakes; the shore is a short pole across the shallows, south.

journal_text: Sal-Sei, Deesh-Duun and Ties-The-Loose-Plank are all dead at the camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge, and I reached none of them in time. I'm to get out through the shallows to the shore below the camp, where the gang's survivors are gathering.
directions: The shore is south of the camp, across the shallows from the burning huts.

journal_text: From the shore below the camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge I watched the light go out of the Hist cutting, whose roots the cutters had already cut from the clutch. The gang's survivors are gathering on the bank, burnt and wet. I'm to stay with them through the night, tend the hurt, and hear at dawn from whoever I saved what became of the clutch.
directions: The survivors sit on the bank below the camp, with the reed bank at their backs; the burnt end of the camp is across the shallows.

journal_text: I got out of the burning camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge with Sal-Sei, the clutch-keeper. At dawn he went back to the shed and came back grey; the eggs under the cut roots are dead and the cutting has withdrawn. The roll burned in the fire, so nobody can say what I owe, and nobody can say what I do not.

I got out of the burning camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge with Deesh-Duun, who saw the woman with the knotted cord as closely as I did. At dawn the gang said the roots were cut and the clutch is dead and Sal-Sei with it, and the cutting has withdrawn. The roll burned in the fire, so nobody can say what I owe.

I got out of the burning camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge in the rowboat with Ties-The-Loose-Plank. At dawn the gang said the roots were cut and the clutch is dead and Sal-Sei and Deesh-Duun are lost, and the cutting has withdrawn. The roll burned in the fire, so nobody can say what I owe.

I got out of the burning camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge alone. Sal-Sei, Deesh-Duun and Ties-The-Loose-Plank are dead, and at dawn Dives-Without-A-Rope told me the roots were cut and the clutch is dead and the cutting has withdrawn. The roll burned in the fire, so nobody can say what I owe.

At dawn the camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge is a ruin and I came out of the fire burnt. The cutting is withdrawn and the uxith is dark. Wuleen-Sei has taken the barge and the unhurt down the coast. Two strangers with a boat, who say a friend of the courier's sent them, are taking off the hurt. Before I go with them I'm to read what the cutters left in the shed, and I may dive for whatever the courier took down into the shallows.
directions: The shed stands beside the withdrawn cutting at the camp's far end; the shallows where the courier went down lie below the burnt boards; the strangers' boat is drawn up on the shore below the camp.

journal_text: The strangers took the hurt by boat to a house in Lilmoth that a fish-trader, Salts-The-Catch, keeps. In the back room, behind a screen, a woman who calls herself Nesh-Deeka sits by the mats, and the one I pulled from the fire lies on one of them. I'm to tell her what I saw at the camp, and get the survivor to tell it too.
directions: The house has no mark; the back room is past the front room's table, behind the screen.

journal_text: Nesh-Deeka is of the Veiled Reed. The roll burnt at the camp, so nobody can show what I owe or that I was on it, and almost no one knows my face: she wants a hand like that. She offers the Reed's protection, this house's door and a stipend, if I serve the Reed. She wants the survivor kept near as a witness; the survivor wants to go home. I'm to answer her on both.
directions: Nesh-Deeka keeps behind the screen in the back room; the mats are beside it.

journal_text: I slept in the house in Lilmoth with the camp's sap still on my tongue, and dreamed. I stood in fog among a ring of trees whose roots climbed up and up, and at the top was a gap like a door that nobody has built. A dry voice spoke that I could not place. I'm to climb to the door.
directions: The roots of the ring climb from the fog to the door-gap at the top.

journal_text: I woke in the house in Lilmoth with a dry anger that passed. I have taken the Veiled Reed's oath: Nesh-Deeka says no one will come asking what I owe, the house's door is open to me, and she put the first of a stipend in my hand.

I woke in the house in Lilmoth with a dry anger that passed. I have taken no oath. The house's door is not mine, but Nesh-Deeka, if she lives, says the Reed will send for me when it has work, and pay for it.

Nesh-Deeka sent me east of Lilmoth to Low-Reed Village, where the Hist has turned its face. The Reed has a hand, Zaren-Ish, in a boat off the village, who wants whoever did it. The root-herald does not like strangers from Lilmoth. I'm to win her leave to see the tree.
directions: The root-herald keeps the platform at the Hist's foot; the jetty is on the village's west side.

journal_text: The tending-ground at Low-Reed Village is closed, the Hist dark and its leaves shut, and the uxith is dark, as it was at the camp. The village says the leeches did it. I'm to go down to the water at the tree's roots and see for myself.
directions: The roots run down from the tending-ground into the water under the stilts; the cut root is the lowest.

journal_text: A root of the Hist was cut at the ring and sealed with black gum, the gum of the village's own sap-workshop, whose knife-peg is empty. The leeches only came to the weeping sap. Pays-Late, the tree-minder, is the one the village blames. I'm to find out what he knows.
directions: Pays-Late goes down to the cut root after dark; the egg-tender keeps the uxith by day.

journal_text: Black gum drips run north from the workshop through the reeds to the leech water, where Pays-Late lost them. I'm to cross the water, find the drips again and follow them to whoever took the tree's sap.
directions: The leech water lies north of the village where the reeds open; past it the reed stems are bent toward a dry rise two cells out.

journal_text: I have the jars of the Hist's sap from the cell's camp in the north reeds. I'm to take them back to the cut root. If I took one of the two men alive, I can bring him before the village, or pole him out to Zaren-Ish's boat.
directions: The cut root is under the stilts; Zaren-Ish's boat lies on the open water off the jetty.

journal_text: I brought the cell's man bound before Low-Reed Village with the cord at his wrist, and the jars were poured back at the cut root. The village knows now who cut its tree, and that Pays-Late did not. The Hist's light is coming back, low and slow. The village has taken me in.

I brought the jars back to Low-Reed Village and they were poured at the cut root. With his own knife back from the cell's camp, Pays-Late is believed: it was strangers' work, not his keeping. The Hist's light is coming back, low and slow. The village has taken me in.

I poled the cell's man out to Zaren-Ish's boat, and the Veiled Reed has him. The jars were poured at the cut root and the Hist's light is coming back, but the village saw a stranger's boat take a man off its water, and the root-herald is cold to me.

I took what I found at Low-Reed Village back to Nesh-Deeka at the Veiled Reed's house in Lilmoth. She says the trees and Nisswo of Helstrom must hear it from someone the Reed can deny, and that the Reed will put me on the coast ship from Lilmoth's stop to Helstrom's river landing, where two of its escorts will meet me. I'm to hear her out and go to the ship.
directions: The Reed's house is the unmarked one among the stilts; the coast ship lies at Lilmoth's stop on the east side, where the ship door stands at the end of the boardwalk.

journal_text: I boarded the coast ship at Lilmoth's stop for Helstrom. The voyage runs along the coast and up the river channels; the ship's other stops are the ordinary travel of the coast. I'm to ride it to Helstrom's river landing, where the Reed's two escorts will meet me.
directions: The ship sets down at Helstrom's river landing, the long timber landing below the city's thorns; there is a trapdoor on the deck to another ship that the Reed's escorts keep clear of.

journal_text: The coast ship set me down at Helstrom's river landing, where two of the Veiled Reed's escorts met me and kept clear of the trapdoor to the other ship. They say the basin round Helstrom kills what walks in it, and the city's gate says it again. I'm to walk inland with them to the city and be led to the hall by the first street.
directions: From the landing the thorned causeway runs north inland between the thorn hedges, raised above the basin; the city's gate stands where the causeway ends among its first houses.

journal_text: In Helstrom the escorts took me to the Hall of the Scalded Throne by the first street, where the state's formal seat is lodged and largely ignored. The Scalded Throne is a plain seat of root and reed at the hall's end, with no dais, and the hall's sweeper sweeps it with a broom. The city sells in the room before it. I'm to look at the seat, speak to the sweeper, Weighs-The-Small-Debt, and go on to the grove by the hall where the Nisswo and the tree-minder are to sit.
directions: The Hall of the Scalded Throne is the low-roofed house by the first street, on the left as the causeway comes in; its inner room holds the seat and its outer room the merchants. The grove is the small stand of root at the hall's east end.

journal_text: In the grove by the hall in Helstrom, Kaska-Meen the tree-minder and Ei-Tuja the Nisswo dispute what happened at the first Hist. She holds an outside hand cut the trees and the tree-minders alone must watch them; he holds that a Hist's turning is its own act, to be read, not clamped. Neither has heard it from one who saw both trees. I'm to hear each, and then say what I saw.
directions: The grove is the small stand of root at the hall's east end, with a young Hist at its middle; the two sit under it, and a few of the city stand round.

journal_text: In the grove in Helstrom I have heard both sides: Kaska-Meen's case that tree-minders alone must watch the trees, and Ei-Tuja's that a Hist's turning is its own act. What I saw at the camp's cut roots and at Low-Reed Village's Hist is what neither of them has. I'm to answer them: side with the tree-minders, side with the Nisswo, or say that a Hist turning and a Hist cut are two things.
directions: Kaska-Meen and Ei-Tuja sit under the young Hist at the grove's middle.

journal_text: In the grove in Helstrom I told Kaska-Meen that tree-minders alone must watch the trees, and she gave her leave to guide me to the city's trees herself. Ei-Tuja was silent. The Veiled Reed's file will say I failed the Reed. The escorts have gone from the landing.

In the grove in Helstrom I argued to Kaska-Meen and Ei-Tuja that a closed tree is to be read, not clamped, and Ei-Tuja gave me the reading freely, as the Nisswo do, and asked nothing for it. Kaska-Meen yielded without yielding. The Veiled Reed's file will say I half served it. The escorts have gone from the landing.

In the grove in Helstrom I told Kaska-Meen and Ei-Tuja that a Hist turning and a Hist cut are two things, and showed them what I saw at the camp's cut roots and at Low-Reed Village's Hist. Both gave a half; the city now knows the Veiled Reed sent me. The escorts have gone from the landing.
Kaska-Meen is dead in Helstrom, and the Tree-Minders will not speak to me or to the Veiled Reed. Ei-Tuja gave his reading alone. The escorts have gone from the landing.
Ei-Tuja is dead in Helstrom, and the debating house where he lodged is cold to me. Kaska-Meen heard me alone. The escorts have gone from the landing.

Root-Herald Ixo-Vaal of Greenspring asked me, for the Many-Root Conclave, to find out why the village's Hist is sickening. The village blames the salt works upstream. I'm to test the water before I believe them.
directions: The fork lies a short walk upstream of the river landing; the herald's house, with the salt sack at its door, faces the Hist.

journal_text: The salt in Greenspring's spring is not coming down the river. The couriers say the Hist's roots run into the flooded galleries of the Drowned Stair. I'm to go down and take water at each landing.
directions: From Greenspring take the road to the Gate-Side Camp outside Helstrom's gate; the guides there show the stair's mouth, where the deep water starts.

journal_text: The water in the Drowned Stair grows saltier the deeper I go. I'm to reach the deepest chamber, beyond one breath, and see where the salt comes in.

Deep in the Drowned Stair, a channel has been cut by hand into a brine seam, and the floods push the brine into Greenspring's roots. The cut is old. I'm to learn who made it, and Vees-Wai, the tree-minder, reads the old stakes.

Greenspring's founders cut the channel to kill a rival grove downstream, and their deed is killing their own Hist. Ixo-Vaal has called the office-holders to the Hist. I'm to put what I found before them and argue for a cure, and for whether the founders are named.
The office-holders of Greenspring sealed the founders' cut and named the deed at the Hist. The tree should mend, and Greenspring now owes the people of the dead grove an answer.
The office-holders of Greenspring sealed the founders' cut and agreed to say nothing of who made it. The tree should mend.
Greenspring chose to reopen the founders' cut downstream. Their Hist is spared, and the dead grove's land will flood with brine again.
